the Drosophila model can be used to study the role of individual dopaminergic and serotoninergic neurons in circuits that determine behavioral output, to understand how disease-associated mutations affect dopaminergic and/or serotonergic neuronal development, to test the efficacy of therapeutic strategies and to perform drug screening.

the development of Drosophilla as a model organism to study the function of dopaminergic and serotoninergic systems in health and disease.
the identification of genes that regulate dopaminergic and serotoninergic neuron development.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying dopaminergic and serotoninergic neurotransmission in Drosophilla melanogaster.
